approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps every accepted score in a task-local archive for a fingerprint Gaussian process, but allows only the sixty-four highest-scoring accepted molecules to remain in its breeding population. It samples parents from three preferred score bands, generates a fresh pool through graph crossover and mutation, and selects evaluations using correlated posterior draws. Accepted offspring immediately compete for survival and can breed in later batches. This gives a functioning learning loop, while chemically distinct lower-scoring parents can disappear from the breeding population before their descendants are explored.
approach.novelty: Allocate survivor places in rounds across molecular cores: the best member of each core competes in the first round, the second-best members in the next, and so on until the existing population is full. Within a round, higher real scores win; the final survivors return to score order for the existing parent sampler. This protects several accepted core families while retaining the incumbent. The recorded lineage has tested posterior selection of generated offspring; this experiment changes the accepted molecules available for future breeding, with the inherited parent-draw rule intact.

hypothesis: Retain accepted breeding molecules by successive score-ordered rounds across Murcko cores, prioritizing each core's best member before any core's next member, then restore global score order for the unchanged parent sampler.

finding_summary.headline: Core-round survival broadened breeding, but protected records never bred and all three score replicas fell.
finding_summary.insights:
Preserving a low-ranked core and exploring it are separate events under the unchanged sampler. Of the 542 protected offspring, 116 survived into a later breeding state, but all remained below the sampled score bands. Six were still retained when the experiment ended and had first received protection in the terminal batch. The broader breeding came through changes to stronger analogues and the ranks of other survivors, rather than descendants of the directly protected records. A local support-promotion trace confirms that this indirect route can produce a parent-beating child, but such participation did not offset the overall loss in productive evaluations.

The actual trajectory also changes the apparent opportunity: on the already diversified Child states, only two incoming molecules were rescued from immediate greedy rejection, while 1,058 newcomers that local greedy selection would accept were excluded. Both rescued newcomers stayed outside breeding support. This narrows the result to a strong redistribution of survivor competition, with little evidence for the hoped-for exploration of protected weak parents. Mean generating-parent strength and mean offspring score both fell, so the smaller average parent deficit is not evidence of better candidates. The molecular assessment still finds repeated oversized heterocycle assemblies, tiny fragments, reactive bonds and constrained ring systems. Core coverage increased without resolving those chemical limitations. The passive greedy lists use existing labels only; they provide no alternate descendants or scores for an independently executed search.
finding_summary.results:
All 4,365 retention calls matched the declared core-round rule, preserved the incumbent and respected the 64-member capacity. Among 3,540 capacity-limited contests, 1,606 changed the local greedy survivor set and added one represented core; 1,266 also changed the immediate breeding support. Mean cores actually used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 24.20, and all fifteen final populations contained 64 distinct cores. There were 12,012 actual parent uses outside greedy breeding support reconstructed from the same accepted history. Those uses contributed to 326 evaluated offspring, including 35 best-parent beats and two incumbent gains.

The direct protection route remained unused: none of the 602 records retained against local greedy eviction, including 542 evaluated offspring, subsequently entered the breeding bands. Overall strict best-parent beats fell from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 526/4,350 (12.09%), and incumbent gains fell from 218 to 175. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.514684, a paired change of -0.029690. All three seed deltas were negative, as were all five task means. The retention mechanism and changed breeding support are confirmed; the intended score improvement was not observed.

molecular.headline: Large repeated aromatic assemblies coexist with compact but reactive carbonyl, amine and fluorinated ring families
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete paired Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9138 to 0.9862 and ring-closure presence from 0.9644 to 0.9908. Charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These counters report SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, actual ionization or feasible stereochemistry. The output spans compact aza-lactams and aryl carbonyl compounds, large aromatic heterocycle assemblies, polyamines attached to constrained rings, expanded cyclic dicarbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl polycycles. Tiny fragments coexist with extensive repeated-module growth. This is especially visible in deco_hop, with mean SMILES length 105.0 and maximum 242; high and final molecules contain many linked aromatic or nitrogen-dione units. Compared with the Parent, broad chemical themes persist while ring topology and substituents change. N-F, peroxides, cumulene imines, unusual sulfur bonding and unspecified ring junctions remain material limitations. Overall synthesis is questionable and drug-like quality weak, although some conventional carbonyl and amine subseries are much more plausible than the extreme products. Diversity across seeds is moderate, with related families dominating late output.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecule is a moderately sized aryl-substituted aza-lactam with alkyl groups and an O-linked cumulated imine side chain. Other high members are fused oxygen/nitrogen heterocycles carrying aryl thioester, ketone or amide groups. Seed 2 retains indole-carboxamide and fused lactam relatives. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9793 and halogen presence is 0.8184. The core carbonyl/heteroaromatic chemistry is recognizable, but N-O bridges, cumulene imines and unusual fused-ring arrangements complicate complete synthesis. Compared with the Parent ketone/amide and sulfur-containing ring families, the successful region still centres on bounded aromatic carbonyl structures.
liabilities: Cumulated imine, N-F and thioester functionality introduces reactivity or stability concerns despite familiar carbonyl fragments.
Constrained oxygen/nitrogen ring fusion, occasional peroxide-containing relatives and tiny fragmented products limit chemical coherence.
missing_features: Stable alternatives to the cumulated imine and N-O-containing fused linkages are underrepresented around the favorable aryl/carbonyl arrangement.
Configurations of stereogenic lactam or fused-ring centres and geometric isomers are unspecified; a unique required target fragment cannot be inferred.

Fluorinating its terminal imine nitrogen gives 0.41930905650182426. Other current seeds have lower maxima than their paired Parents, although fused aryl thioester and ketone members reach 0.4238198477630873 and 0.4207408531749377. The evidence favors the complete aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over fragment-sized products and does not show a general need for reactive nitrogen fluorination.

Linker length, saturation and nitrogen placement are tolerated to differing degrees; the modest variation does not identify a uniquely required target fragment.

Leaders often contain N-F as well as carbon-bound fluorine; methylated and N-Cl relatives are also present. Other seeds produce acyclic urea/formamide/enamine arrangements or fused phenolic nitrogen-carbonyl systems. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9138 and halogen presence is 0.6092. transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest extremes include small hydrocarbon/halogen fragments and repeated multiaryl or nitrogen-dione products. One set has mean SMILES length 105.0 and maximum 242; large coupled products elsewhere reach scores as low as 1.6758614448245604e-53.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide compact recombination, linker shortening and removal of duplicated modules while preserving useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine attachment patterns. Repeated growth should not dominate the alternatives to an intact favorable scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leaders and close relatives contain cumulated imines, N-F/N-Cl, aryl peroxides and multiply substituted sulfur with a carbon-sulfur double bond. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand stable matched nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur and carbon linkages, and represent chemical compatibility independently of scalar feedback. Different local score preferences make general stable-alternative generation more useful than assuming every high-scoring reactive group is necessary.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 throughout despite aryl-substituted lactams, branched polyamines, saturated amino-bearing rings and fluorinated bridged imines. Dense fusion and constrained unsaturation occur repeatedly among leaders.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces constrained and stereogenic ring systems without resolving their configurations or accessible geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support accessible ring-size and fusion alternatives plus consistent configuration assignment and stereoisomer variation. The current unspecified molecules cannot establish stereochemical score sensitivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cyclic-sulfide ring variants share 0.6112877583465819; ordinary versus cumulated unsaturation variants share 0.6087949743003997. A shorter-linker cyclic dicarbonyl at 0.21350507156602996 is close to its longer-linker counterpart at 0.21523191119058618.
transferable_gaps.gap: Simplification remains underexplored in favorable regions that already tolerate ring and linker changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate simpler stable ring, linker and substituent variants around established arrangements. Such variants can make score-tolerant regions more chemically interpretable and accessible without naming or requiring a particular objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

Preserving a low-ranked core and exploring it are separate events under the unchanged sampler. Of the 542 protected offspring, 116 survived into a later breeding state, but all remained below the sampled score bands. Six were still retained when the experiment ended and had first received protection in the terminal batch. The broader breeding came through changes to stronger analogues and the ranks of other survivors, rather than descendants of the directly protected records. A local support-promotion trace confirms that this indirect route can produce a parent-beating child, but such participation did not offset the overall loss in productive evaluations.

The actual trajectory also changes the apparent opportunity: on the already diversified Child states, only two incoming molecules were rescued from immediate greedy rejection, while 1,058 newcomers that local greedy selection would accept were excluded. Both rescued newcomers stayed outside breeding support. This narrows the result to a strong redistribution of survivor competition, with little evidence for the hoped-for exploration of protected weak parents. Mean generating-parent strength and mean offspring score both fell, so the smaller average parent deficit is not evidence of better candidates. The molecular assessment still finds repeated oversized heterocycle assemblies, tiny fragments, reactive bonds and constrained ring systems. Core coverage increased without resolving those chemical limitations. The passive greedy lists use existing labels only; they provide no alternate descendants or scores for an independently executed search.

finding_summary.headline: Core-round survival broadened breeding, but protected records never bred and all three score replicas fell.
finding_summary.insights:
Preserving a low-ranked core and exploring it are separate events under the unchanged sampler. Of the 542 protected offspring, 116 survived into a later breeding state, but all remained below the sampled score bands. Six were still retained when the experiment ended and had first received protection in the terminal batch. The broader breeding came through changes to stronger analogues and the ranks of other survivors, rather than descendants of the directly protected records. A local support-promotion trace confirms that this indirect route can produce a parent-beating child, but such participation did not offset the overall loss in productive evaluations.

The actual trajectory also changes the apparent opportunity: on the already diversified Child states, only two incoming molecules were rescued from immediate greedy rejection, while 1,058 newcomers that local greedy selection would accept were excluded. Both rescued newcomers stayed outside breeding support. This narrows the result to a strong redistribution of survivor competition, with little evidence for the hoped-for exploration of protected weak parents. Mean generating-parent strength and mean offspring score both fell, so the smaller average parent deficit is not evidence of better candidates. The molecular assessment still finds repeated oversized heterocycle assemblies, tiny fragments, reactive bonds and constrained ring systems. Core coverage increased without resolving those chemical limitations. The passive greedy lists use existing labels only; they provide no alternate descendants or scores for an independently executed search.
finding_summary.results:
All 4,365 retention calls matched the declared core-round rule, preserved the incumbent and respected the 64-member capacity. Among 3,540 capacity-limited contests, 1,606 changed the local greedy survivor set and added one represented core; 1,266 also changed the immediate breeding support. Mean cores actually used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 24.20, and all fifteen final populations contained 64 distinct cores. There were 12,012 actual parent uses outside greedy breeding support reconstructed from the same accepted history. Those uses contributed to 326 evaluated offspring, including 35 best-parent beats and two incumbent gains.

The direct protection route remained unused: none of the 602 records retained against local greedy eviction, including 542 evaluated offspring, subsequently entered the breeding bands. Overall strict best-parent beats fell from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 526/4,350 (12.09%), and incumbent gains fell from 218 to 175. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.514684, a paired change of -0.029690. All three seed deltas were negative, as were all five task means. The retention mechanism and changed breeding support are confirmed; the intended score improvement was not observed.

The audit distinguishes protection of an existing record from rescue of a newly arriving record. Across 1,606 local-greedy disagreements, 602 distinct records are protected at least once: 542 accepted offspring and 60 initial observations. The offspring account for 1,255 protection occurrences. After first protection, only 116 of the 542 offspring persist into a later resolved breeding state, and none ever reaches the top-half support, is actually selected as a parent or produces a scored descendant from a post-protection use. All 60 protected initial records likewise have zero post-protection support/use; 19 persist into a later state. Thus the direct protected-parent-to-descendant route is unobserved for every task and seed. Protected offspring persist for a mean 2.76937269373 retention calls including the first protection, range 1 to 95. Six remain in final memory and first received protection during the terminal batch, so their post-retention breeding opportunity is censored by the end of evaluation. The other protected records must not be described as explored families merely because they temporarily survive.

Only two incoming accepted molecules are immediately retained when local greedy selection would reject them, among 538 incoming local-greedy rejections. Both are acyclic: seed-0 zaleplon C=CF scores 0, persists from admission serial 73 through serial 81 and is evicted at 82; seed-1 deco_hop CCC(Br)CCl scores 0.5, persists from serial 77 through 90 and is evicted at 91. Both are observed in later survivor states but remain outside breeding support and never breed. Conversely, 1,058 incoming molecules that local greedy survival would admit are excluded by core rounds. This differs from the passive Parent opportunity of rescuing 1,008 rejected newcomers because the actual Child is already operating on a diversified evolving population.

A separate cohort explains one actual route to changed use: 486 records (480 offspring and six initial records) are locally promoted into the first-32 support when a stronger extra analogue is removed; the promoted records themselves survive under both local rules. These records account for 1,266 local support-promotion occurrences. After first promotion, 173 later remain in support and 145 actually breed, in 399 uses, all unavailable in same-history greedy support at those draws. Four produce direct scored descendants after promotion and one has a descendant that beats its actual generating parents. These are not the locally protected weakest records. A seed-0 sitagliptin example promotes initial serial 7 at admission 70; it is later used 14 times and participates in a batch-7 child scoring 0.244144232682 against best actual parent 0.238550671735. This supports an indirect rank/exclusion route, without a score for the passive parent pairing.

Across all actual generation, 326 accepted offspring have at least one generating parent unavailable under greedy support on the same accepted history. They include 35 strict parent beats, 147 immediate admissions, two incumbent gains and 66 offspring later bred; mean child-minus-best-parent is -0.149984301692. The other 4,024 accepted offspring contain 491 beats, 2,609 admissions and 173 incumbent gains, with mean delta -0.0901985141866. These selected-parent strata differ in task, age, state and score and are not randomized causal comparisons. All offspring, parent uses and direct/transitive scored descendants are joined to the actual provenance, including proposals from the changed support that never survive or breed.

Overall the Child has 526/4,350 strict best-parent beats (0.120919540230), fewer than the Parent's 565, with mean child-minus-best-parent -0.0946790122847. It admits 2,756 offspring, later breeds 1,870 distinct offspring in 104,188 parent-use events, and has 1,172 offspring with direct scored descendants. Incumbent gains fall to 175; same-core offspring fall to 1,559. Mean ancestry depth is 8.44919540230, maximum 22. Mean best-generating-parent score falls to 0.392078439014 and mean evaluated-offspring score to 0.297399426729. Therefore the less-negative relative deficit does not establish stronger candidate production. Seed beat counts are 180,179,167 of 1,450, versus 194,189,182; mean deltas are -0.0928143334408, -0.101648005304 and -0.0895746981091.

possible_failure_causes: The direct route from protecting a record against local greedy eviction to exploring its descendants is unsupported: all 602 protected records remain outside later breeding support, even though the overall survivor and breeding distributions change.

The fixed high-score bands prevent protected low-ranked records from being sampled. Of 542 protected offspring, only 116 even persist to a later breeding state, and six terminal retained records have no later generation opportunity.

Core-round competition excludes 1,058 newcomers that local greedy selection would accept while rescuing only two otherwise rejected newcomers on the Child's evolved states. This may remove productive analogues; the missing alternate offspring scores prevent a separate causal estimate.

Mean parent strength and mean evaluated-offspring score decline, parent-beating yield drops, and incumbent gains fall from 218 to 175. A less-negative relative parent deficit does not overcome the negative paired final-score result.

Murcko diversity retains coarse scaffold differences while ignoring stereochemical and many peripheral distinctions. The molecular assessment still finds repeated growth, reactive bonds and difficult ring geometries, so increased core counts do not establish useful chemical diversity.

Only three paired replicas and the supplied five-task panel are observed. The full-identity acyclic metadata branch runs but its records never breed; extraction-fallback behavior has no runtime opportunity in these data.

applicability_conditions: Confirmed for the supplied five objectives and seeds 0,1,2 with 300 evaluations per task, batch ten and 64 bounded survivors; all labels are finite accepted observations from the current objective session.

Meaningful retention opportunities occur at 3,540 over-capacity local contests. The 825 initial or under/at-capacity calls retain all eligible records; no single-core contest tests that reduction branch.
The actual rule only sees current survivors plus the sequentially accepted newcomer. It never restores a discarded archive molecule; full-history greedy comparisons are passive and label-preserving.

All non-retention interfaces remain fixed, including complete accepted archive, canonical identities, serial/origin records, pending provenance, parent quantile selection, graph generation, posterior inference and within-pool acquisition.

The retention rule has confirmed downstream support and actual-parent-use changes, but protected-record retention is not itself an explored-family outcome. None of the directly protected records reaches later support; the observed route involves exclusion and score-rank changes among other survivors.

Core keys retain scaffold atom and bond types and omit stereochemical distinctions. Acyclic accepted identities remain separate groups, with no acyclic breeding use here; no extraction fallback is observed.

The changed support participates in scored descendants, but overall yield and all three macro scores decline. Passive greedy lists and probability laws provide no separately evaluated alternate trajectory or missing oracle label.

finding_summary.headline: Core-round survival broadened breeding, but protected records never bred and all three score replicas fell.
finding_summary.insights:
Preserving a low-ranked core and exploring it are separate events under the unchanged sampler. Of the 542 protected offspring, 116 survived into a later breeding state, but all remained below the sampled score bands. Six were still retained when the experiment ended and had first received protection in the terminal batch. The broader breeding came through changes to stronger analogues and the ranks of other survivors, rather than descendants of the directly protected records. A local support-promotion trace confirms that this indirect route can produce a parent-beating child, but such participation did not offset the overall loss in productive evaluations.

The actual trajectory also changes the apparent opportunity: on the already diversified Child states, only two incoming molecules were rescued from immediate greedy rejection, while 1,058 newcomers that local greedy selection would accept were excluded. Both rescued newcomers stayed outside breeding support. This narrows the result to a strong redistribution of survivor competition, with little evidence for the hoped-for exploration of protected weak parents. Mean generating-parent strength and mean offspring score both fell, so the smaller average parent deficit is not evidence of better candidates. The molecular assessment still finds repeated oversized heterocycle assemblies, tiny fragments, reactive bonds and constrained ring systems. Core coverage increased without resolving those chemical limitations. The passive greedy lists use existing labels only; they provide no alternate descendants or scores for an independently executed search.
finding_summary.results:
All 4,365 retention calls matched the declared core-round rule, preserved the incumbent and respected the 64-member capacity. Among 3,540 capacity-limited contests, 1,606 changed the local greedy survivor set and added one represented core; 1,266 also changed the immediate breeding support. Mean cores actually used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 24.20, and all fifteen final populations contained 64 distinct cores. There were 12,012 actual parent uses outside greedy breeding support reconstructed from the same accepted history. Those uses contributed to 326 evaluated offspring, including 35 best-parent beats and two incumbent gains.

The direct protection route remained unused: none of the 602 records retained against local greedy eviction, including 542 evaluated offspring, subsequently entered the breeding bands. Overall strict best-parent beats fell from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 526/4,350 (12.09%), and incumbent gains fell from 218 to 175. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.514684, a paired change of -0.029690. All three seed deltas were negative, as were all five task means. The retention mechanism and changed breeding support are confirmed; the intended score improvement was not observed.

molecular_assessment.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete paired Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9138 to 0.9862 and ring-closure presence from 0.9644 to 0.9908. Charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These counters report SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, actual ionization or feasible stereochemistry. The output spans compact aza-lactams and aryl carbonyl compounds, large aromatic heterocycle assemblies, polyamines attached to constrained rings, expanded cyclic dicarbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl polycycles. Tiny fragments coexist with extensive repeated-module growth. This is especially visible in deco_hop, with mean SMILES length 105.0 and maximum 242; high and final molecules contain many linked aromatic or nitrogen-dione units. Compared with the Parent, broad chemical themes persist while ring topology and substituents change. N-F, peroxides, cumulene imines, unusual sulfur bonding and unspecified ring junctions remain material limitations. Overall synthesis is questionable and drug-like quality weak, although some conventional carbonyl and amine subseries are much more plausible than the extreme products. Diversity across seeds is moderate, with related families dominating late output.
